text:
caroline: Heads-up: planning SDK v6.0.0 tomorrow 09:30 PT. Key change: consolidate retry/backoff settings and make idempotency tokens required for non-idempotent generation calls. Also introducing a client-side circuit-breaker default to protect both customers and our clusters.

sam: Required idempotency tokens? That sounds breaking for users who just call generate() without extras.

caroline: Behavior: for most simple use cases we provide a migration shim that auto-generates an idempotency token when none is provided, but it will log a NOTICE and we strongly recommend apps pass explicit tokens. After 120 days the SDK will require explicit `idempotency_key` for calls that have side effects (uploads, fine-tune triggers, non-deterministic writes). Generate/text endpoints will keep shim for 6 months only.

patrick: What exactly is being consolidated for retry/backoff? We have retry_max, retry_ms, backoff_factor scattered across SDKs.

caroline: We are consolidating to a single `retry_policy` object: {"max_retries": int, "base_delay_ms": int, "max_backoff_ms": int, "jitter": boolean}. Old flat keys will be accepted by the shim and mapped to the new object with a single deprecation log per process. The runtime default will be more conservative: max_retries reduced from 5 -> 2, base_delay_ms 100 -> 200, jitter ON by default.

ops-bot: CI note: deploy window reserved 09:30-10:00 PT. Docs linter rule added: RETRY_POLICY_CONSOLIDATION (docs-601) and IDEMPOTENCY_TOKEN_REQUIRED (docs-602). Both WARN for 14 days then ERROR.

sam: Circuit-breaker defaults? Will this cause early failures?

caroline: Circuit-breaker is local client-side only: trip threshold defaults to 10 failures in 60s per host, cooldown 120s. This prevents aggressive retries against degraded endpoints. Teams can tune via `client.circuit_breaker` config or disable it with env var `RWI_ALLOW_AGGRESSIVE_RETRY=true`.

docs-bot: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/678 "docs: retry policy consolidation, idempotency tokens, client circuit-breaker" Includes migration recipe + code snippets for Python/JS/Go. Linter IDs: docs-601, docs-602.

patrick: Hosted API side - do we require server-side idempotency headers?

caroline: Hosted API will accept both behaviors for 30 days. We will honor `Idempotency-Key` header when present. After 30 days public endpoints may log warnings and then enforce for certain write endpoints. For Dedicated/Private we will not change server-side enforcement unless the tenant enables it.

legal: Quick note: ensure migration doc clarifies that auto-generated tokens are not equivalent to explicit customer-provided tokens for dedup guarantees. Add exact wording.

support: Please prepare KB explaining: how to add idempotency_key, how to tune new retry_policy, and how to opt into old behavior temporarily.

caroline: Will do. release-bot will publish internal checklist and changelog. Draft changelog: "SDK v6.0.0  retry_policy consolidation, idempotency_key guidance and shim (6mo for generate, 120d for write endpoints), client-side circuit-breaker defaults, linter schedule, rwi-cli helpers." Internal checklist: https://internal.redwood/releases/checklists/sdk-6-retry-idempotency

sam: Any CLI helpers for scanning repos?

caroline: Yes: `rwi-cli scan-retries --report` and `rwi-cli inject-idempotency --dry-run|--fix`. They ship in `rwi-cli@1.2.0`. The inject tool will add a generated key comment and optionally add a deterministic key snippet for tests.

patrick: Sounds reasonable. I'll run the scan tonight and open follow-ups for quick fixes.

caroline: Thanks. I'll post a short email to #all at 09:00 PT with timeline and links. Ping me if you spot edge cases.

support: ACK. We'll draft the KB and get it reviewed.
